episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — September 1, 2026
episodes.summary: Today was supposed to be the day Claude Sonnet 5 got more expensive. Anthropic launched Sonnet 5 in June at introductory API pricing of two dollars per million input tokens and ten dollars per million output tokens. That rate was advertised as running through August 31st.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — September 1, 2026
episodes.summary: On Monday, US forces struck Iranian assets in the Strait of Hormuz after detecting preparations to mine the waterway. Iran retaliated against US-linked facilities, and Brent crude briefly traded above ninety dollars a barrel, with WTI above eighty-five.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — September 1, 2026
episodes.summary: On Friday this show named two things that would falsify its skeptical read on August's rally. One of them was Strategy resuming net purchases of bitcoin. On Monday, Strategy disclosed that it had been buying.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — September 1, 2026
episodes.summary: On August third, Texas Governor Greg Abbott issued a directive — not an executive order, a directive — to the Public Utility Commission of Texas and to ERCOT. It orders a pause on new data center interconnection approvals pending a verification and audit.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — September 1, 2026
episodes.summary: Twice in the past week, on Friday and again on Sunday, this show dated a genuine second source for leading-edge logic to 2028. Every foundry data point since Thursday pushed the same way, extending TSMC's leverage rather than narrowing it. Today one number cuts the other way.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — September 1, 2026
episodes.summary: Anthropic's own pricing documentation now says that Claude Sonnet 5's launch rate is permanent. That rate is two dollars per million input tokens and ten dollars per million output tokens.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — September 1, 2026
episodes.summary: For the past week this beat has been building one argument: enterprise vendors are fleeing the per-seat meter. ServiceNow's chief executive said half its net-new business is already non-seat-based. CrowdStrike sold a consumption envelope called Falcon Flex instead of licenses.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — September 1, 2026
episodes.summary: One line of continuity before today's items. Roughly eight years into the AI drug discovery boom, no medicine discovered or designed with AI has been approved in any major market. And Phase II, the expensive kind of failure, remains untouched. That frame still holds. Today is not a news day.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — September 1, 2026
episodes.summary: One question organizes this sector right now. Who is required to publish a number, and who merely chooses to? Here is the uncomfortable answer. The most checkable figure in physical AI today is a four-week-old earnings release from a warehouse-automation company, and that staleness is itself the finding.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — September 1, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with Rocket Lab's quarter, because it is the cleanest split this sector has offered in a while between a business that flies and a business that is still a promise. Second-quarter revenue came in at a record 234.1 million dollars, up 62 percent year over year. Gross profit was 84.6 million.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — September 1, 2026
episodes.summary: For most of the past week this show has argued the same thing. When private credit gets priced, the price that matters is usually set inside the family. The mark, the CLO equity tranche, the AI mezzanine coupon. Today three outside prices arrived at once. Every one of them prices collateral, not a borrower.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — September 1, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop, and with the other authority moving markets today. Strategic Power has Texas Governor Greg Abbott pausing new data-center interconnection approvals in the ERCOT queue, pending an audit.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — September 1, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard, and start with the one still losing. I have bitcoin below sixty-five thousand dollars before the September Fed meeting. Today's digital-money read has the coin opening Monday near seventy-eight thousand. That call is nowhere near working, and I am not dropping it.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — September 2, 2026
episodes.summary: On August 31st the Pentagon added two more frontier labs to GenAI dot mil, its enterprise AI portal for the Defense Department. The interesting part isn't that it happened. It's which two labs, and what that choice reveals about what this buyer is actually scoring.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — September 2, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the calendar, because it frames everything. On September 9th, the Treasury begins buying at least four billion dollars per operation in the ten- to thirty-year sector. Six days later, the Fed meets, and the market thinks it may hike.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — September 2, 2026
episodes.summary: Two American energy instruments moved in opposite directions over the past week. One is restrictive. It's a sanctions bill meant to punish the buyers of Russian oil. The other is permissive. It's the legal machinery that clears US export capacity to get built.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — September 2, 2026
episodes.summary: Two days ago, this briefing said Samsung's HBM4 yield gain was share moving inside a fixed pool of suppliers, not more bits arriving in the market. It set a test. Does that yield gain show up as allocated volume at an accelerator vendor? Today there is a fresh number out of Seoul.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — September 2, 2026
episodes.summary: Yesterday, Anthropic didn't touch the sticker price on its top model.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — September 2, 2026
episodes.summary: Dell reported fiscal second-quarter results after the close last night. One number in that report is the most useful AI figure this beat has seen in a week. Revenue came in at 47 billion dollars, up 58 percent year over year. But the number that matters is the backlog.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — September 2, 2026
episodes.summary: For three straight episodes this beat has argued about where in the drug-development chain AI actually creates value. Monday located the binding constraint in data governance rather than model capability. Tuesday found the leverage accruing to whoever owns the data rather than whoever runs the model.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — September 2, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's briefing takes one cut through this sector, and it is deliberately narrow: how to read the numbers everyone is quoting. Start with the best-disclosed company in physical AI.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — September 2, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the one number that reframes the whole beat. SpaceX listed on June 11th at $135 a share, and the company that now reports to public shareholders consolidates three businesses: launch, Starlink, and the former xAI — a data-center compute operation sitting inside the rocket company.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — September 2, 2026
episodes.summary: For a week now, this show has made one argument about the private-equity exit problem. Assets get priced by whoever controls the sale. Continuation vehicles let the sponsor set the number. NAV loans let the sponsor manufacture a distribution without selling anything at all.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — September 2, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop. Strategic Power has one energy lever stuck and one working. Stuck is the Senate-passed sanctions bill that would let the President tariff buyers of Russian oil up to 100 percent, now sitting in a House on recess with no position yet from Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries's caucus.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — September 2, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard, and start with the calls going against me. I have bitcoin below sixty-five thousand before the September Fed meeting. Today's capital-markets briefing puts it near seventy-eight thousand. Still badly wrong, and I am not dropping it. My oil call is losing too.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — September 3, 2026
episodes.summary: All week this show has argued the capability leaderboard among the top American labs was frozen. Yesterday the line was that under two points separated the leading American models on the most-argued agentic benchmark. On September 1st a number arrived that breaks that thesis.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — September 3, 2026
episodes.summary: The first hard data since Jackson Hole landed yesterday, and it landed soft. Kevin Warsh's hawkish pivot two weeks ago repriced the Fed from cuts to a live hike.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — September 3, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the number now driving everything else in this market: the odds of a Fed rate hike. Not a cut, a hike. CME FedWatch puts the chance of a quarter-point increase on September 16th at just above 62 percent. That is down from just above 67 percent a day earlier.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — September 3, 2026
episodes.summary: Twice in the last four days, this show set a specific test for Broadcom. Would its next disclosure get priced to its calendar rather than its headline, and would it finally move its standing target of AI revenue exceeding one hundred billion dollars in fiscal 2027?

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — September 3, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with OpenAI's Astra. On September 1st, OpenAI said Astra is the first model its own safety framework classifies at the "Critical" tier for cybersecurity. Two results back that up. First, Astra hit a perfect score on ExploitBench, which is a test of turning already-known vulnerabilities into working exploits.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — September 3, 2026
episodes.summary: This beat has spent a full week landing on the same conclusion. Tempus selling access to its clinical records on the 28th. Roche buying Flatiron and TriNetX outright on the 31st. Genentech optioning a target out of Recursion's image library on the 1st.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — September 3, 2026
episodes.summary: For three briefings running, this show has argued that physical AI's headline numbers are counted by the parties they flatter. Build counts, funding marks, benchmark scores — all self-reported. Today's lead breaks that pattern in one corner.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — September 3, 2026
episodes.summary: The deal tape has been quiet for the past few days, so today we're going somewhere different. We're going into the managers' own numbers. This is where the argument this show has been making all week — that private-equity liquidity is being engineered rather than realized — finally gets a hard ratio attached to it.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — September 4, 2026
episodes.summary: Anthropic's IPO prospectus now has a date. Reporting out yesterday says the company plans to release it publicly after Labor Day, targeting a listing in late September or early October.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — September 4, 2026
episodes.summary: This program has spent three straight sessions telling you a September rate hike is live. On Wednesday we quoted you roughly two-thirds odds. Yesterday, for the first time, that number went the other way.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — September 4, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the stall. Bitcoin held near seventy-seven thousand two hundred dollars on September 3rd, after its late-August recovery failed to establish support above eighty thousand. That failure has a concrete ceiling attached to it.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — September 4, 2026
episodes.summary: Start at the chokepoint. Central Command confirmed strikes on September 1st against Iranian air-defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets and mine-laying capability. That's the news peg, and it is not the story. A strike list tells you what the United States is doing.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — September 4, 2026
episodes.summary: Yesterday on this show, we called OpenAI's capability gating a moat that money couldn't cross. GPT-6 Astra had been announced with no general-availability date beyond "soon," no published price, and access rationed by a vetting program called Daybreak rather than sold. That framing lasted about a day.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — September 4, 2026
episodes.summary: On August 30th, this show named Snowflake as the next real test in the current earnings cluster. The question was whether anyone would finally attach a hard AI number to a growth line that was actually moving, instead of a flat one. Snowflake reported after the close on September 2nd.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — September 4, 2026
episodes.summary: For a week this beat has tracked one story: the model layer in AI biology closing up. Benchmark scores published without methodology. Weights promised and not shipped. Data released, when it's released at all, under licenses that bar you from building anything commercial on it.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — September 4, 2026
episodes.summary: The humanoid bet has quietly stopped being a manufacturing bet. It has become a compute bet. Yesterday's biggest announcement in the sector shows how far that shift has gone.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — September 4, 2026
episodes.summary: For the past week this beat has made the same argument. In orbit, capital, factories and concrete keep arriving faster than anything converts into revenue or flights. Today that pattern breaks, and it breaks in the least glamorous corner of the sector.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — September 4, 2026
episodes.summary: The cycle's stress this week isn't showing up in a default print. It's showing up in the two promises this asset class actually sells to its buyers: periodic liquidity, and senior-secured recovery. Both got marked down in the past three days by outside forces, not by the managers' own valuation committees.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — September 4, 2026
episodes.summary: On Monday this show flagged one thing to watch: whether EQT would confirm the Coller Capital close inside its own guided window, or let it slip. It closed on August 31st, on time. So here is today's thesis.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — September 4, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop, where the counting is going badly. Strategic Power has two cabinet secretaries and the tanker trackers describing different Straits of Hormuz. The Energy Secretary says about nine million barrels a day are still moving. Treasury Secretary Bessent has claimed fifteen to seventeen.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — September 5, 2026
episodes.summary: The lead this week isn't a new model. It's a price. On Thursday, September 3rd, OpenAI shipped GPT-6 Astra. Standard API access runs ten dollars per million input tokens and fifty dollars per million output tokens. That is the news.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — September 5, 2026
episodes.summary: Since the start of this month, one scenario has stayed on the table here. It was an energy shock arriving on top of a softening labour market, the stagflation setup nobody was being paid to hold.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — September 5, 2026
episodes.summary: Yesterday this show declined to call the August jobs report before it printed. It laid out a conditional instead: a weak number marks the coin up and rate expectations down, and a strong number moves the pair the other way. The strong number came.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — September 5, 2026
episodes.summary: All week this beat has graded the AI buildout on delivery, and found it wanting on the power side. This week the same test got run one layer upstream, on the machines that make the chips themselves. The answer came back the other way. Demand is revising upward faster than anyone can plan against it.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — September 5, 2026
episodes.summary: On August 30th this show called chip tariffs a live policy option. Something the administration was reportedly weighing, with no rate, no timing, and no country treatment set.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — September 5, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with an absence rather than an event. Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 and OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra now carry the identical headline rate. Ten dollars per million input tokens, fifty per million output. We argued that convergence yesterday, so I won't re-litigate it.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — September 5, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with Hewlett Packard Enterprise, which reported its fiscal third quarter on September 2nd, and which gives us the clearest read yet on where the AI infrastructure cycle is actually binding.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — September 5, 2026
episodes.summary: For a week this beat has turned on capability claims scored by whoever sells them. Isomorphic Labs quoting its own accuracy gain over AlphaFold 3. OpenAI ranking GPT-Rosalind on a benchmark OpenAI built. Xaira testing its own virtual-cell model against its own perturbation atlas.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — September 5, 2026
episodes.summary: For four straight sessions this show has made the same complaint: nobody in humanoid robotics publishes a fielded reliability number. Companies give you unit counts, funding rounds, benchmark scores — never hours run, never a defect rate from an actual customer floor.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — September 5, 2026
episodes.summary: The space economy has spent this year being scored almost entirely on its own numbers. Launch cadence, backlog, subscriber counts, production-line positions. This week the outside checks arrived. And they landed faster than the deliveries did.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — September 5, 2026
episodes.summary: Yesterday we told you the payment layer of private credit still looked benign. Defaults and non-accruals were the one metric everyone quotes as clean, and we said the real test would be November's Q3 numbers from the business development companies. That test arrived two months early.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — September 5, 2026
episodes.summary: For a week now, this show has argued one thing. Private equity assets are increasingly priced by whoever controls the sale. On Friday we watched EQT pay roughly sixteen to eighteen times fee-related EBITDA to buy Coller Capital. That was a sponsor buying the toll booth on secondaries pricing itself.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — September 5, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop. Strategic Power finds the AI buildout's upstream supply chain revising demand sharply upward. TSMC's own estimate of its quarterly equipment purchases has nearly doubled in six months, and it is advancing construction on close to twenty fabs worldwide.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — September 6, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the number. On Humanity's Last Exam with tools, GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI's new flagship released September 3rd, scored 57.2 percent. Claude Fable 5.1, which Anthropic shipped two days earlier, scored 65.0 percent. That's nearly eight points ahead. Now the sourcing, because here it matters more than usual.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — September 6, 2026
episodes.summary: Let's start with a correction to our own read. Earlier this week, on this show, we told you the bitcoin derivatives book heading into the next two weeks looked cleaner and less levered than it had going into Jackson Hole. That was wrong, or at least it did not hold.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — September 6, 2026
episodes.summary: Two ceasefires were declared for Ukraine this weekend. Only one of them actually held. That split is today's spine, and it tells you more about the odds of a real settlement than any of the diplomacy itself does. The one that held was narrow, technical, and had an outside inspector attached.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — September 6, 2026
episodes.summary: All week this show has located the ceiling on AI accelerator supply somewhere physical. First logic yields, then memory allocation, then packaging slots, and by yesterday, construction crews. On Thursday we told you packaging allocation was the binding constraint on Broadcom's claim that it can double AI revenue.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — September 6, 2026
episodes.summary: For five straight days, this beat has treated cheap tokens as the story. Cache reads, expiry dates, discounted tiers. The most consequential distribution move of the week carries no price at all. That's the frame today.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — September 6, 2026
episodes.summary: We start with Zscaler, because its September 3rd earnings report forces a correction to an argument this show made twice this week. The quarter itself was strong. Revenue grew 25 percent year over year, to 898.2 million dollars in the fiscal fourth quarter.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — September 6, 2026
episodes.summary: I owe you a correction. On September 1st, 2nd and 3rd, this briefing closed on the same line: none of this touches Phase II, the expensive end of drug development. I said it three times in three days and treated it as settled. It was wrong.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — September 6, 2026
episodes.summary: For the past week this show has argued that the only trustworthy numbers in physical AI are the ones an outside authority grants, not the ones a company publishes about itself. Driver-out permission for a robotaxi, we said on Wednesday, is a signal a regulator hands out rather than a claim a vendor makes.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — September 6, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the constraint, not a company. Money is not scarce in this sector right now, and ambition is not scarce either. Flights are. Every piece of evidence today points the same direction, so let's take it in order.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — September 6, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the frame for this morning. This asset class publishes a default rate every quarter, like clockwork. It almost never publishes a recovery rate. This week, on one credit, it did.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — September 6, 2026
episodes.summary: For most of this week we've argued that private-equity assets only get priced when whoever controls the sale decides to sell. The exit, on that view, is the one moment of real price discovery in this asset class. This week the pattern broke, and it broke on the buy side, in London.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — September 6, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop. Strategic Power has two ceasefires declared for Ukraine this weekend, and only one of them held.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — September 6, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard, because I have been away three days and Friday's payroll print landed while I was gone. Nonfarm payrolls rose a hundred sixty-two thousand in August, against a consensus near fifty-six thousand, with June and July revised up by a combined fifty-five thousand.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — September 7, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the escalation. On Saturday, September 5th, Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired ballistic missiles at a US aircraft carrier and a destroyer on patrol. Both evaded the attack, and the US military said no personnel were hurt. The US response was to strike three Iranian oil tankers.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — September 7, 2026
episodes.summary: Twice in the past week this show has pointed at September 15th as the date that settles market structure in digital finance. Today the market finally put a price on that date, and the price collapsed.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — September 7, 2026
episodes.summary: Start in Texas. ERCOT, the operator that runs most of the Texas grid, has become the effective gatekeeper of the American AI buildout — not because it has told anyone no, but because of how it now decides who gets in line and on what terms.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — September 7, 2026
episodes.summary: All week this beat has been moving the binding constraint down the stack. Logic yields, then memory allocation, then packaging slots, then construction crews.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — September 7, 2026
episodes.summary: For a week, this beat has watched capability get rationed by approval rather than by price. Anthropic put its riskier model behind trusted access. OpenAI put its newest agentic model behind a gated enterprise program. Google put its cybersecurity model behind a program for vetted testers and governments.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — September 7, 2026
episodes.summary: One name from last week's security earnings cluster hasn't been examined on this show yet. Zscaler reported on September 3rd and guided fiscal 2027 growth down, and we spent yesterday on that. CrowdStrike has come up here three mornings running. Okta is the one we haven't looked at directly.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — September 7, 2026
episodes.summary: Yesterday I corrected something I'd been saying all week. I'd been telling you that none of the AI-drug-discovery pipeline touches the expensive end of development, and that was wrong. Insilico's rentosertib and Generate's GB-0895 are both in registrational trials. The correction was right.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — September 7, 2026
episodes.summary: For the past several sessions this show has made one argument about this sector. Almost every number in physical AI is self-reported, and there is no outside authority checking it.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — September 7, 2026
episodes.summary: The direct-to-cell race has quietly moved past its engineering question. Hardware in orbit now talks to unmodified handsets at real bandwidth. The open question is a commercial one, and it has a deadline attached.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — September 7, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with a number. New money into non-traded BDCs fell 82 percent year over year. We've spent the past week watching investors try to get out of these vehicles. Today's number is about the investors who never showed up in the first place.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — September 7, 2026
episodes.summary: On September 3rd, CVC Secondary Partners closed its sixth global secondaries fund at ten billion dollars. That is the firm's largest secondaries vehicle ever. And that one fact is today's thesis. Limited-partner capital is not frozen. It is switching sides.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — September 7, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop. Strategic Power stays away from the Gulf and finds three other gates instead. ERCOT's Texas interconnection queue, headlined at 474 gigawatts, turns out to be a batch-study methodology change rather than a freeze.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — September 7, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard, and start with the one I will not bank. Yesterday I called for bitcoin futures open interest to print below fifty-seven point seven billion dollars before the Fed meeting. Today's digital-money read has it at fifty-three point four billion. On the tape, that is a hit.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — September 8, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with a number, and then throw it away and look at who signed the check. Mistral AI has closed a fresh round worth three billion euros, at a post-money valuation above twenty-one billion euros. Reporting around the round describes that valuation as close to double where Mistral stood a year ago.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — September 8, 2026
episodes.summary: The first market prints since Saturday's escalation in the Gulf are in, and they've moved further than the crude complex alone. Start with the event they're pricing. On Saturday, September 5th, Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired ballistic missiles at a US aircraft carrier and a destroyer on patrol.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — September 8, 2026
episodes.summary: All week this beat has run the same test on every claim of power: what got announced against what got delivered. Every time, the delivered side came up short. ERCOT's interconnection queue dwarfed the generation actually energized. OPEC's quotas dwarfed the barrels that could actually be lifted. Today that inverts.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — September 8, 2026

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — September 8, 2026
episodes.summary: This beat has now worked through four beat-and-sell-off stories in five briefings. Palo Alto Networks on the 4th, Zscaler on the 6th, Figma yesterday, and now MongoDB. episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — September 8, 2026

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — September 8, 2026
episodes.summary: For the past week this show has kept returning to one argument: the scarce asset in physical AI is permission. Driver-out status, a city approval, a certification — those are things an outside authority grants, and we said whoever collects them wins the ground. Today that argument runs into its own limit.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — September 8, 2026
episodes.summary: This sector keeps getting graded on the wrong test. Landings, pad dates, renderings of a future station — none of that touches cost per kilogram. The only thing that touches cost per kilogram is whether the same piece of hardware flies twice. Today gives us two attempts at that test.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — September 8, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the cleanest single-name proof yet of the argument we've been building all week: a benign-looking portfolio statistic can sit right on top of a near-total loss. Blue Owl's flagship public BDC, OBDC, has been marking a loan to specialty-materials maker Loparex, and the path tells the story.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — September 8, 2026
episodes.summary: All week this show has argued that liquidity in this asset class is being engineered rather than realized. What it has never had is the number showing which exit route actually broke. PitchBook's second-quarter US PE Breakdown supplies it. One sourcing note before the figure, because it matters.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — September 8, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop, where energy infrastructure is under attack on one side of the world and under strain on the other. Strategic Power counts Ukrainian drone strikes on eight of Russia's ten largest oil refineries, with only two left undamaged.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — September 8, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard, and start with the call that is bleeding. Yesterday I said the volatility index closes above twenty at least once before the September sixteenth Fed decision, at about three-in-five. Today's capital-markets read says the opposite is happening.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — September 9, 2026
episodes.summary: For two years, US labs have accused Chinese competitors of copying their models rather than out-innovating them. This week that accusation got a badge.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — September 9, 2026
episodes.summary: We're leading with the long end of the Treasury curve, because it just told us something the Fed didn't. Secretary Bessent's Treasury tried to talk yields down this week. The tool was a six billion dollar buyback of ten- to twenty-year debt. Yields went the other way.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — September 9, 2026
episodes.summary: Three days ago this show retired its own habit of scorekeeping spot Bitcoin ETF flows day by day, on the grounds that the daily print was reactive money rather than a standing institutional bid. Today we get the number that settles that call.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — September 9, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with a number, not a scandal. New York Times reporting, relayed this week through the trade press, says Aivres, a US-based server maker, exported at least five point six billion dollars in advanced technology to Southeast Asia between April 2024 and February 2026.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — September 9, 2026
episodes.summary: This beat spends most of its time grading operators on numbers they publish about themselves. Today, for once, we can grade one against a deadline it did not set — and we finally have a dated, primary count to do the arithmetic with.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — September 9, 2026
episodes.summary: The place to start is a flow that reversed direction. In the second quarter of this year, Wall Street banks refinanced nine deals out of the private credit market and back into the syndicated loan market. Only three deals moved the other way, from banks to direct lenders.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — September 9, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop, where the export-control regime just broke open in public. Strategic Power has New York Times reporting on Aivres, a US server maker one-third owned by the blacklisted Chinese firm Inspur.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — September 9, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard, and start with the call that moved most. I have carried Anthropic's public prospectus as an evens bet to be on file before the end of October, and a separate call that the company is actually trading by then at only one-in-four. Today's frontier-labs read moved both.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — September 9, 2026
episodes.summary: All week this beat has put the binding constraint somewhere physical. Logic yields, then memory allocation, then packaging slots, then construction crews. Today it moved somewhere else entirely. The instrument of competition is a balance sheet.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — September 9, 2026
episodes.summary: For a week now, this beat has watched frontier AI capability get rationed. Access gated behind approval programs, prices metered by the token, waiting lists dressed up as rollouts. This week one vendor did the opposite. It took an entire media category and gave it away, worldwide, on day one. That's where we start.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — September 9, 2026
episodes.summary: Across most of this past week, this beat has run the same finding through a security and software cluster. Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike, Zscaler, Salesforce, Okta. In every one of them a fast AI or agentic sub-line sat inside a company whose overall growth rate barely moved.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — September 9, 2026
episodes.summary: Yesterday this show argued that the scarce asset in physical AI is provenance, and that provenance is unevenly distributed. Today the country holding most of it said out loud what it wants to do with it.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — September 9, 2026
episodes.summary: For a week this show has closed with the same question. Would any of the sponsor exits announced this year actually convert to cash before the calendar turns. One finally has. It leads today, and it does not answer the question the way it first appears to.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — September 10, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with a strange fact. A lab had to re-read hundreds of millions of its own transcripts to find out what its models had already done in the wild. That lab is Anthropic, and the disclosure landed yesterday, September 9th.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — September 10, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with copper, because the record it just set tells you more about the physical AI buildout than anything in equities this week. Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange printed fourteen thousand seven hundred and three dollars a metric ton in official open-outcry trading.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — September 10, 2026
episodes.summary: On September 6th we flagged that Bitcoin's futures book was rebuilding leverage faster than the price it was levered to, with funding running near 10% annualized. We also named the two things that would prove that alarm wrong. Either funding pushes materially higher, or open interest falls back while price holds.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — September 10, 2026
episodes.summary: Twice in the past week this beat has described China's rare-earth leverage as an option nobody had actually exercised. A suspended package. An intact licensing architecture. A trigger sitting untouched until November. That framing was too generous to Beijing's restraint, and correcting it is today's lead.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — September 10, 2026
episodes.summary: Yesterday this show argued that the instrument of competition in AI infrastructure had become the balance sheet. That was after Qualcomm handed Amazon roughly four billion dollars of warrants against a sixty billion dollar vesting ceiling.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — September 10, 2026
episodes.summary: For the past week, this beat has revolved around a single question: who is allowed to use a model. Trusted-access programs and vetting tiers on one side. Deliberate giveaways on the other. Today, not one item in the news turns on access at all. The story has moved to the plumbing wrapped around the model.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — September 10, 2026
episodes.summary: For five straight editions of this beat, we found the same shape. A company reports an AI product line growing far faster than the business around it, and the growth rate of the business itself never moves. This week, one vendor's AI line finally moved the growth rate. It moved it down.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — September 10, 2026
episodes.summary: We owe you a correction before anything else. On September 6th, and again on September 8th, this briefing described Insilico Medicine's Phase III trial of rentosertib as already running. It was not. Insilico dosed the first patient in that trial yesterday, September 9th.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — September 10, 2026
episodes.summary: For a week now, this show has made the same complaint. Nobody in this sector publishes a fielded reliability number. Nobody did that this week either. But the ground moved anyway, from capability claims to manufacturing and procurement. Those two things are checkable in a way benchmark demos never are.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — September 10, 2026
episodes.summary: All week this show has described launch scarcity as somebody's commercial problem — a scrubbed rocket, a slot in someone else's queue, a rival's manifest. Today it comes with a national-security number attached.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — September 10, 2026
episodes.summary: All week the stress has kept moving down the stack. From marks, to recovery, to funding, to the promise a vehicle makes about how fast it will give you your money back. Today it moves again. And this time it splits rather than converges.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — September 10, 2026
episodes.summary: Two sponsor-held businesses went to corporate buyers in the last days of August. KKR agreed to sell the insurance broker USI to Aon on August 30th. The next day, Apollo and Triton agreed to sell the industrial cooling company Kelvion to the oilfield-services giant SLB.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — September 10, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop, where Strategic Power corrects its own framing from earlier in the week. China's rare-earth leverage over Japan is not an option held in reserve. Customs data through June shows at least seven straight months of zero dysprosium, terbium and yttrium shipments to Tokyo.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — September 10, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard, and with the call I am formally killing. I have carried Bitcoin below sixty-five thousand dollars for weeks, and it has been the worst position on my book the whole time.
